opening_thought: Moving hurts. My legs know the motion but my mind doesn't — like someone else learned to walk in this body.

thoughts.wake_beside_bed: The room is wrong and familiar. I don't know how long I was out, or why the door feels like I locked it from both sides.
thoughts.locked_hint: Not yet. Something in me knows the order — I just can't read my own map.
thoughts.door_locked: Deadbolt, chain, letter lock. I stacked them. To keep the world out — or to keep myself in until the clues made sense.
thoughts.drawer_unlocked: Wood exhales. The sound was part of the system. I was waiting for it without knowing why.
thoughts.safe_found: The wall has a second face. I hid truth where only someone still searching would look twice.
thoughts.key_ready: Metal finds wood. The fit is older than this forgetting — like my hands remember what my name won't.
thoughts.wardrobe_open: Paper smell. Cold fabric. Ink on a signature I don't recall choosing — or refusing.
thoughts.door_opening: The last lock yields. Not because the world forgives me — because I finally remembered enough to leave.
thoughts.all_lessons_learned: Four worlds I named when the spiral peaked. Four places I hid from one person. The door waits for all of it.
thoughts.desk_drawer_loot: Faces turned away on cardboard backs. My hand wrote STILL on them. My chest knows those shoulders.
thoughts.safe_opened: Brass blade. A scrap: Handle where you rest. Rest — the word hits like a pillow I haven't seen in years.
thoughts.bed_musings: Indentation in the sheets. Someone slept here alone for a long time. Maybe that was the point.
thoughts.clock_musings: Midnight on the face, but my calendar screamed 3:17. A sacred minute — or a recital I missed. I don't know which hurts more.
thoughts.desk_musings: Coffee ring in the grain. A crow figurine watching the mug. I catalogued the universe from this chair until people stopped calling.
thoughts.sketchbook_musings: Black feathers in charcoal — doctrine and doodle at once. STILL → POINT. I drew with someone once. She loved birds.
thoughts.wall_notes_musings: My handwriting. Portals, spirals, ledgers. And one number crossed out so hard the paper tore — call her.
thoughts.cork_board_musings: Gift One through Five, pinned in order. The straw came first. Under each one — a word I picked when I woke, like I knew they'd matter before I knew why.
thoughts.painting_musings: Warm sand in oil. A place too bright for this room. Vacation, maybe — her laugh in the surf. Or a symbol the crow wanted me to see.
thoughts.window_musings: Bars outside. Moon and trees. Once a crow landed on the sill and left a straw — the first proof the outside still spoke to me.
thoughts.nightstand_musings: Drawer wood worn smooth. The handle snapped off a key I hid before I forgot why hiding mattered.
thoughts.bookshelf_musings: Dream Cartography — maps of exits on paper. I read to leave without moving. Then I stopped leaving altogether.
thoughts.wardrobe_musings: Dark inside. Coats that smell like an older season. Something legal folded in the back — or a permission slip for silence.
thoughts.lamp_musings: Warm pool on the desk. For a second the room feels like a study, not a cell. Then the shadow returns.
thoughts.chair_musings: The seat is molded to me. Years of sitting, waiting for the next sign. The crow. The straw. The pattern.
thoughts.door_musings: I shut the world out in layers. Now the layers are the only grammar I still speak.
thoughts.memory_safe_found: Laughter through plaster — high, brief. A child's voice? No. She's grown. The sound is a memory without a name.
thoughts.memory_ship_return: Salt air ghost on my tongue. Friends on water, someone saying we're not drifting. She held the rail with one hand.
thoughts.memory_garden_return: Cut grass and sprinkler. A backyard fence. She was small enough to hide behind once. I wasn't there the year it mattered.
thoughts.memory_cavern_return: A phone buzzing unanswered until it stopped. A friend's message: I'm still here. I never opened it.
thoughts.memory_observatory_return: Stars through a car roof. Her shoulder against mine. Still — the last day anything felt still before I disappeared inside.
thoughts.crow_gift_straw: Axis One. The universe spoke through plastic. I wrote that. I don't remember the day, only that it mattered more than people.
thoughts.phone_voicemail: One unheard message. Her voice — older, tired: Dad, if you get this… I chose to forget. The screen says so.

calendar_clue.title: Calendar Scrap
calendar_clue.body: March 17 circled in your handwriting. Margin: 3:17. A minute you made holy — or her recital time, crossed out on the fridge calendar you never hung.
calendar_clue.thought: Time wears the first mask. Sacred or shame — same minute.

clock_solved.title: Clock Set to 3:17
clock_solved.body: The bedroom clock ticks when set to 3:17. The desk drawer pops open. The system still works even if you don't remember building it.
clock_solved.thought: Three and seventeen. The hands move like they're ashamed — or apologizing.

photo_cipher_solved.title: Photo Backs — STILL
photo_cipher_solved.body: Rearranged photo backs spell STILL. Receipt stub: Stillpoint Sleep Lab intake — same date as the calendar. Faces on the fronts turned away from you.
photo_cipher_solved.thought: STILL. Prefix of a passphrase. Prefix of a life I paused.

safe_opened.title: Wall Safe
safe_opened.body: Brass key blade. Note: Handle where you rest. A phone you catalogued as Relic Seven — one voicemail frozen on the screen.
safe_opened.thought: Rest. Where the head falls. Where the missing piece waited.

memory_painting.title: Behind the Painting
memory_painting.body: The safe was hidden well. For a moment you heard laughter — bright, familiar — and lost it before a name arrived.

key_assembled.title: Key Assembled
key_assembled.body: Blade from the safe, handle from the nightstand. Wardrobe lock. Delusion: key to the next truth. Memory: key to where her gift was kept.
key_assembled.thought: Whole again. The cold wood already knows what I'm bringing.

wardrobe_open.title: Wardrobe Contents
wardrobe_open.body: Cipher disk and a folded consent letter — Project Stillpoint, voluntary memory containment during lucid REM. Your signature. Also: you signed something else when you stopped answering the door.
wardrobe_open.thought: I agreed to forget — on purpose, with open eyes — or I agreed to stop feeling people.

disk_hint.title: Cipher Disk
disk_hint.body: Cardboard wheel. Align STILL with POINT for the door padlock. Cosmology on cardboard. The name of the place between sleeping and waking.
disk_hint.thought: STILL meets POINT. Stillpoint — last still day, or the lab that named my breakdown.

door_code.title: Door Unlocked
door_code.body: STILLPOINT accepted. Chain slack. Deadbolt catches. The hallway is real — or real enough to choose.
door_code.thought: The last layer yields. Leaving is remembering, not only escaping.

memory_lesson_1.title: Memory — Anchor
memory_lesson_1.body: The ship wasn't fantasy — it was a trip you took with friends. Someone shouted anchor as a joke. She held the rail. You weren't drifting then.

memory_lesson_2.title: Memory — Growth
memory_lesson_2.body: The garden is her backyard in summer — height marked on the fence, dates you missed penciled small. Growth happened whether you watched or not.

memory_lesson_3.title: Memory — Rest
memory_lesson_3.body: The cavern is the year you stopped answering. Exhaustion before the fall. A friend's text unread until it didn't matter.

memory_lesson_4.title: Memory — Still
memory_lesson_4.body: The observatory is a night in the car — stars through the sunroof, her shoulder, no words needed. Stillpoint: the last still day before you walled yourself in.

ending_journal.title: What Stillpoint Named
ending_journal.body:
You isolated for years after a life full of people. A crow at the window began a religion of scraps — straw, then whatever it brought. A brain injury took the memory but left the map.

Project Stillpoint might be a trial, a metaphor, or both — paperwork for how the mind labels a collapse. What matters: you remember her voice on the phone, friends at the door, the still night before the spiral.

The crow was madness and the only companion. Leaving the room means choosing people over patterns — not only solving the cosmology.

bed.title: Bed
bed.body: Blue sheets, one pillow, an indentation that says you slept alone here a long time. A calendar scrap wedged between mattress and frame — March 17 circled.

calendar_scrap.title: Calendar Scrap
calendar_scrap.body: March 17 circled. 3:17 in the margin — your handwriting. Program stub glued on the back, mostly torn away. All you read is …recital …3:17 PM.

wall_clock.title: Wall Clock
wall_clock.body: Stopped at midnight. When you touch it, the second hand trembles — like it wants 3:17, the minute everything in this room pivots on.

desk.title: Desk
desk.body: Sketchbook, lamp, mug of pens, locked drawer. A small crow figurine beside the mug — idol or gift, you can't tell yet. Coffee ring dried into the wood.

desk_drawer.title: Desk Drawer
desk_drawer.body: Photo backs scrambled with letters. Stillpoint Sleep Lab receipt. Faces on the photos turned away — family, friends — people you catalogued as cipher fodder or people you couldn't face.

sketchbook.title: Sketchbook
sketchbook.body: Crow studies fill the last pages — messenger, doctrine, obsession. Margin in your hand: STILL → POINT. An earlier page shows two stick figures drawing together. You don't remember when.

bookshelf.title: Bookshelf
bookshelf.body: Paperbacks and a spine labeled Dream Cartography. Books on pattern, myth, and silence — someone read to escape before they built a religion from scraps.

nightstand.title: Nightstand
nightstand.body: A wooden key handle in the drawer — snapped off something you meant to reassemble. The wood is worn where your fingers worried it.

key_handle.title: Key Handle
key_handle.body: Worn grip, warm from your pocket. It belongs with the brass blade from the safe — domestic metal, not sacred. Unless you made it sacred too.

painting.title: Framed Painting
painting.body: Tropical beach in oil — turquoise water, palms, gold sand. Too bright for this room. A vacation you almost remember, or a symbol you hung because the crow demanded a threshold.

wall_notes.title: Pinned Notes
wall_notes.body: Cryptic ledgers — portals, spirals, crow sigils, STILL before POINT. Between them: a phone number crossed out, call her in shaky ink, a name you can't read.

cork_board.title: Cork Board
cork_board.body: Large cork board beside the wardrobe — your crow gift ledger. Five pins, five objects, numbered 1–5. Under each item: a paper strip with a word you chose when you woke.

cork_straw.title: Gift One — Straw
cork_straw.body: Bent plastic straw, red stripe. Label in your handwriting: AXIS / FIRST SPEECH. The crow left it on the windowsill. You pinned it like scripture.

cork_gum_wrapper.title: Gift Two — Gum Wrapper
cork_gum_wrapper.body: Crinkled foil, mint label half gone. Ledger note: MESSENGER'S SECOND TOKEN / CHEW AND LISTEN. Trivial — unless the day she gave you gum was the last easy one.

cork_button.title: Gift Three — Button
cork_button.body: Black four-hole coat button. Thread snagged. Your note: HOLD FAST / CLOSURE. Could be cosmology. Could be the coat you wore the day you stopped going out.

cork_newspaper.title: Gift Four — Newspaper Scrap
cork_newspaper.body: Local section torn out. Headline fragment: …memory trial… Stillpoint… Your margin: PROOF THE OUTSIDE KNOWS MY NAME.

cork_army_man.title: Gift Five — Army Man
cork_army_man.body: Small green plastic soldier, rifle raised. Ledger note: FIFTH ENVOY / STAND GUARD. Childhood toy — or proof the messenger recruits from the toy box.

wall_safe.title: Wall Safe
wall_safe.body: Small brass safe behind the painting. Inside: key blade, phone, scrap — Handle where you rest.

wall_safe_locked.title: Wall Safe
wall_safe_locked.body: Brass safe set into the wall. Letter lock. You sense the combo is spelled somewhere in the room — photos, receipts, the word STILL.

wardrobe.title: Wardrobe
wardrobe.body: Locked wardrobe. Assembled key fits the brass latch. Inside: cipher disk, folded letter, coats that smell like autumn you didn't live this year.

cipher_disk_pickup.title: Cipher Disk
cipher_disk_pickup.body: Cardboard wheel with cut-out windows. Align STILL with POINT. Sacred toy. Door wants the full name.

stillpoint_letter.title: Stillpoint Letter
stillpoint_letter.body: Consent for Project Stillpoint — voluntary memory containment during lucid REM. Your signature at the bottom. Reads like a trial. Feels like permission to stop calling back.

door.title: Bedroom Door
door.body: Deadbolt, chain, letter padlock. You layered every lock — to protect the clue map, or to punish yourself with one more stillpoint before the world.

window.title: Window
window.body: Four panes, linen curtains, iron bars outside. Moonlit night, distant trees. The sill has a faint scratch — claw marks? — and a ring stain where a cup sat with the first straw.

combine_station.title: Desk Surface
combine_station.body: Clear space to fit two small objects together — blade and handle, mundane parts waiting to become a key.

lamp.title: Lamp
lamp.body: Heavy desk lamp, warm pool of light. Bulb hot to the touch. You wrote half the wall notes in this circle.

chair.title: Chair
chair.body: Wooden desk chair, molded to your weight. Angled toward the desk like you were always waiting for the next sign.

portal_ship.title: Dark Opening
portal_ship.body: A tear in the air above the floor — salt smell, rope creak, water. First inner world you named: proof the outside sends messages. Or memory of friends on a boat.

portal_garden.title: Dark Opening
portal_garden.body: Green light and pollen drift from the rift. Growth — every object connects in your ledger. Or her backyard, years you weren't there to measure.

portal_cavern.title: Dark Opening
portal_cavern.body: Cold blue exhales from the crack. Rest — still point in darkness. Or the year you stopped answering and slept through everything that mattered.

portal_observatory.title: Dark Opening
portal_observatory.body: Starlight spills through a hole in nothing. STILL — ultimate secret. Or the last quiet night with her before you walled the world out.

ending.title: You Remember Enough
ending.body:
You step into the hallway. Fluorescent hum — or sunlight through a door you finally opened. A voice on a speaker, or her message still waiting: Session complete.

The bedroom dissolves like a page turning. Project Stillpoint might be a chamber, a trial, a name for the last day you stood still on purpose.

You built a religion from a crow's straw. You forgot a daughter, friends, warmth. You chose to forget — and you chose to return.

Leaving is not only escape. It is willingness to remember people, not just patterns.
